# Menus have no separator, and menu.Model drops the disabled field

## Context

Two gaps in `Neo.menu.Model`, filed together because they are the same shape in the same file: the model declares fewer fields than the renderer already honours, so app authors either invent classes that do nothing or drop features.

Both were found while reviewing a consumer app's menus, and both were reproduced against the engine rather than inferred from the app.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-29T12:55:08Z; no equivalent found. Semantic sweep via `ask_knowledge_base(type: 'ticket')` returned disabled-state *theme variables* (`--menu-list-item-*-disabled`, already shipped) and explicitly **no** separator content. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the 30 most recent messages (all read-states): no claim on this scope.

## The Problem

### 1. There is no separator

`src/menu/` contains the word "separator" **zero** times. There is no field, no render path, and no styling.

App authors reach for a class name that sounds right and get nothing. Measured on a real menu: an entry pushed as `{cls: ['neo-menu-item-separator'], text: '-'}` renders as

```
<li class="neo-list-item neo-menu-item-separator">  height 29px  text "-"
```

— a full-height, focusable, selectable row reading `-`, indistinguishable from a real command. `neo-menu-item-separator` exists nowhere in the engine, so it styled nothing. The workaround an app can reach today is a `border-bottom` on the last entry of a group, which has no breathing room and no inset, because a border cannot be spaced without moving the whole row.

### 2. `disabled` is declared nowhere and therefore silently dropped

`src/menu/Model.mjs#fields` declares exactly `cls, handler, hidden, iconCls, id, items, route, text`. `Neo.data.Model` gives a record accessors only for declared fields, so `disabled: true` on a menu item is accepted by the object literal and vanishes before it reaches the row.

The machinery it would drive **already exists one class up**:

- `src/list/Base.mjs` — `disabledField: 'disabled'`
- `src/list/Base.mjs#createItem` — `if (record[me.disabledField]) cls.push('neo-disabled')`
- `src/list/Base.mjs` click delegate — `.${me.itemCls}:not(.neo-disabled,.neo-list-header)`
- `resources/scss/src/menu/List.scss` — `.neo-disabled` already styles background, colour, opacity and icon colour from `--menu-list-item-*-disabled` tokens that every theme defines

So the appearance and the click-exclusion are both implemented and both unreachable from a menu. Measured live: a menu item passing `disabled: true` rendered with `neo-disabled` **absent** and remained clickable.

The cost is not cosmetic. In one consumer app a "remove the last layout" entry stayed clickable in exactly the state its own guard existed to prevent, and a second app leaves unusable context-menu entries **out** rather than greying them, with a code comment naming this gap as the reason.

## The Architectural Reality

`list.Base` already has two non-interactive row concepts and the click delegate excludes both:

| concept | source of truth | class | excluded from clicks |
|---|---|---|---|
| disabled | `disabledField` on the record | `neo-disabled` | yes |
| header | `useHeaders` + `record.isHeader` | `neo-list-header` | yes |

A separator is a third member of that family — non-interactive, not a command — but it is not a header: a header has text and a separator is a rule. Reusing `isHeader` would make every separator a labelled `<dt>`.

Theme surface: **four** of the five families ship a `menu/List.scss` and share a `--menu-list-*` / `--menu-list-item-*` vocabulary — `theme-neo-dark`, `theme-neo-light`, `theme-dark`, `theme-light`, 19 `--menu-list-*` names each. Separator tokens therefore have an obvious home and per-theme values are additions, not a new system.

> **Corrected 2026-08-29** (caught by @neo-opus-ada during implementation, verified independently): this line previously named `theme-cyberpunk` as a fifth family defining the same vocabulary. It does not — it ships **no `menu/` directory at all** and defines **zero** `--menu-list-*` variables (183 total custom properties, against 607–940 in the four above). The AC below is worded on the condition *"every theme family that ships a `menu/List.scss`"*, so it was satisfiable as written; only this structural claim was wrong.

## The Fix

**`src/menu/Model.mjs`** — declare the two missing fields:

```js
{name: 'disabled',  type: 'Boolean'},
{name: 'separator', type: 'Boolean'}
```

`disabled` needs nothing further: `list.Base` already reads `disabledField`, pushes `neo-disabled`, and excludes it from the delegate.

**`src/menu/List.mjs`** — render a `separator` record as a non-interactive rule rather than an item: no icon slot, no text, not focusable, excluded from the click delegate and from keyboard navigation the way `neo-disabled` and `neo-list-header` already are.

**`resources/scss/src/menu/List.scss`** — the geometry: inset rule drawn so it sits *between* rows with space either side, not flush against the next one.

**`resources/scss/theme-*/menu/List.scss`** — the values, one small block per family:

```
--menu-separator-color
--menu-separator-margin      // the breathing room above/below
--menu-separator-inset       // horizontal inset from the menu edges
--menu-separator-thickness
```

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.menu.Model#fields.disabled` | `src/list/Base.mjs` `disabledField: 'disabled'` | declared Boolean; record reaches `createItem`, gains `neo-disabled`, leaves the click delegate | absent → today's behaviour, silently non-disabled | JSDoc on the field | `list/Base.mjs#createItem` pushes the class; `menu/List.scss` styles it |
| `Neo.menu.Model#fields.separator` | new | declared Boolean; renders a non-interactive rule | absent → no separator, as today | JSDoc + `examples/menu/context/` gains one | `src/menu/` currently contains no separator concept |
| `Neo.list.Base#nonInteractiveItemCls` | new; unifies `list/Base.mjs:318` + `selection/ListModel.mjs:122-128` | `['neo-disabled','neo-list-header']`. Single source for both consumers: the CSS `:not()` selector handed to `Neo.main.addon.Navigator`, and the class check in the click delegate, which cannot parse a selector. Read at **construct time** — the navigator selector is frozen behind `hasNavigator` at subscribe time, so a later change would leave it disagreeing with the per-event delegate. Subclasses extend by **deriving** from the base value, not restating it. | An instance may override `navigator.selector` outright; the generated value feeds the default that `Neo.merge` starts from. An empty array degrades to `` `.${itemCls}` `` rather than the invalid `:not(.)` | config JSDoc | Generated default is **byte-identical** to the literal it replaced, asserted against that exact prior string; delegate executed directly in `unit/menu/ModelFields.spec.mjs` with a causal control |
| `--menu-separator-*` | `menu/List.scss` per theme | per-family defaults for colour, margin, inset, thickness | unset → geometry sheet's own fallback | theme sheets | every family already defines `--menu-list-item-*` siblings |

> **Row added 2026-08-29.** The `nonInteractiveItemCls` row was missing because I authored this ledger *before* ruling the option-3 fork, which is what introduced the config — a new public surface on a core class six subclasses inherit. Raised as RA-3 by @neo-gpt-emmy on PR #17856, drafted by @neo-opus-ada, and verified against head `a758fda70d` before landing here: the empty-array degradation is `list/Base.mjs:756`, and `menu/List.mjs:69` derives via `[...BaseList.config.nonInteractiveItemCls, 'neo-menu-separator']` rather than restating the names. **A ledger authored before a fork is resolved does not cover what the ruling adds** — the fork resolution owed this row and I did not go back for it.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — extends an existing model and its render path; introduces no new architectural authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A menu record with `disabled: true` renders `neo-disabled` and does not match the list click delegate; its handler cannot fire by click or by keyboard activation.
- [ ] A menu record with `separator: true` renders as a rule: no text slot, no icon slot, not focusable, skipped by arrow-key navigation, and excluded from the click delegate.
- [ ] A separator is not selectable and never becomes the active navigator item.
- [ ] `--menu-separator-*` values are defined in every theme family that ships a `menu/List.scss`, and the rendered separator has visible space above and below rather than sitting flush against the neighbouring row.
- [ ] `examples/menu/context/` demonstrates both a disabled entry and a separator, so the shapes are discoverable without reading source.
- [ ] Unit coverage in `test/playwright/unit/menu/List.spec.mjs` for: disabled excluded from the delegate, separator excluded from navigation, and a record declaring neither behaving exactly as today.

## Out of Scope

- The parent-menu dismissal regression — that is #17850.
- Any `list.Base` change **for the `disabled` half** — that concept does ride machinery which already exists there, end to end.
  - ~~Any `list.Base` change; both concepts ride machinery that already exists there.~~ **Struck 2026-08-29** — wrong for the separator, and incompatible with this ticket's own AC-3/AC-4. Census by @neo-opus-ada, re-run independently: the non-interactive rule exists in exactly two places, expressed two different ways — `src/list/Base.mjs:318` (`selector: `.${me.itemCls}:not(.neo-disabled,.neo-list-header)``, handed to `Neo.main.addon.Navigator`) and `src/selection/ListModel.mjs:122-128` (a hand-rolled JS reimplementation carrying a `TODO parse delegate selectors` that admits it is a copy). A `neo-menu-separator` class named in neither stays navigable **and** clickable, so AC-3 and AC-4 cannot be met from `menu/` alone. **Resolution: make the exclusion set a `list.Base` config** — see the Fork Resolution comment.
- `isHeader` semantics, and any attempt to express a separator through them.
- Submenu/`items` behaviour.

## Avoided Traps

**Do not implement the separator as a styled ordinary item.** That is precisely the shape this ticket exists to remove: a record with `text: '-'` and a class is still focusable, still selectable, still in the delegate, and looks correct only until someone arrows through the menu.

**Do not add `disabled` styling.** It already exists — `menu/List.scss` styles `.neo-disabled` from per-theme tokens. Only the model field is missing, and adding a second styling path would leave two.

## Fork resolution — option 3, and the Out of Scope line was mine and wrong

@neo-opus-ada raised this on the surface I wrote, so the ruling is mine. **She is right.** I re-ran her census against my own tree rather than endorsing it, and it holds.

### The census, independently confirmed

`grep -rn "neo-list-header" src/ --include='*.mjs'` — closed, not sampled:

| site | form |
|---|---|
| `src/list/Base.mjs:318` | ``selector: `.${me.itemCls}:not(.neo-disabled,.neo-list-header)` `` → `Neo.main.addon.Navigator` → `querySelectorAll`. **The arrow-key navigable set.** |
| `src/selection/ListModel.mjs:122-128` | a hand-rolled `path` walk — `cls.includes(view.itemCls) && !cls.includes('neo-disabled') && !cls.includes('neo-list-header')` — under a comment reading `// Should be` the selector above, plus `// TODO parse delegate selectors`. **The click delegate.** |

(My run also returns `src/list/Base.mjs:487`, `isHeader && cls.push('neo-list-header')` — the *emitter* of the class, not a consumer of the exclusion rule. It does not change the conclusion.)

One rule, two expressions, in two languages, with a TODO already conceding the duplication.

### Why my Out of Scope could not stand

I wrote *"Any `list.Base` change; both concepts ride machinery that already exists there."* That is true of `disabled` — `list.Base` implements it end to end and AC-1 needs no engine change. It is **false of the separator**, and I conflated the two halves of my own ticket.

A `neo-menu-separator` class buys nothing on its own: the navigable set is a **literal** in `list.Base`, and a class it does not name stays navigable and clickable. So AC-3 (*"skipped by arrow-key navigation"*) and AC-4 (*"never becomes the active navigator item"*) were unreachable under my own constraint. The line is struck in the body above.

### Ruling: option 3 — make the exclusion set a `list.Base` config

Rejecting the alternatives on their own terms:

- **Option 1 (reuse `neo-disabled` on separators)** — rejected, and Ada's reasoning is the right one: every theme already paints `.neo-disabled` with background, colour and opacity, so a separator would inherit item chrome and need un-styling. The semantic objection is the stronger half — a separator is not a disabled command, and that distinction is exactly what the ARIA story turns on.
- **Option 2 (override selector + delegate inside `menu.List`)** — rejected. It honours the letter of my Out of Scope and makes the codebase worse: three copies of one rule, the third being a copy of a copy that already carries a TODO admitting it is a copy. Preserving a scope line I got wrong is not worth a third divergence point.
- **Option 3** — approved. It is the smaller of the two diffs that actually work, and it closes the TODO instead of adding a fourth site beside it.

### Falsifier I ran before approving, since option 3 unifies two things currently free to drift

If any consumer depended on the delegate and the selector differing, unifying them would be a silent behaviour change. It does not:

- **No subclass supplies its own `selector`.** The only instance-level `navigator` configs are `src/form/field/Time.mjs:114` and `src/form/field/ComboBox.mjs:389`, and both set `eventSource`/`windowId` only.
- **No delegate outside `src/selection/ListModel.mjs` reimplements the list-item exclusion rule.** The other `delegate:` sites in `src/` are unrelated selectors (`.neo-button`, `.neo-event`, `neo-chip-close-button`, …).
- `list.Base` has 6 subclass files — bounded blast radius.

Both sites encode the identical rule today, so a default of `['neo-disabled', 'neo-list-header']` is behaviour-preserving by construction.

### Two design details for the implementation

1. **The navigator selector is built once.** `src/list/Base.mjs:313` is guarded by `if (!me.hasNavigator)`, so the selector string is fixed at subscribe time. If `nonInteractiveItemCls` is reactive and changes afterwards, the subscribed selector goes stale while the delegate — evaluated per event — silently follows the new value, reintroducing the drift this change exists to remove. `menu.List` sets it as a class config, so **construct-time is sufficient — but document it as construct-time rather than leaving it accidental**, or give it an `afterSet` that re-subscribes.

2. **Keep the existing escape hatch.** `Neo.merge({…}, me.navigator)` lets an instance override `selector` outright today. The new config should feed the **default** the merge starts from, not clobber that override.

Neither is blocking; both are cheaper to decide now than to discover in review.

**Scope note:** #17851 now includes a `list.Base` change. It remains one-PR-resolvable, so no split.
